root_cause_gate.trigger: A real run_tests call held the command auto-lock for about 29.5 seconds, was then auto-failed against a 15-second job-creation clock, and later emitted genuine TestRunner callbacks.
hypotheses: StartedUnixMs is incorrectly used as the AwaitingRunStarted clock even though synchronous Execute and semaphore delay occur before that state.
Callbacks mutate the global current job rather than a persisted physical owner identity.
Command-scoped auto-lock cleanup releases run_tests protection when the job-start response completes, before the physical TestRunner run terminates.
The upstream clear_stuck parameter is indistinguishable from an unfiltered start to the private guard and lock classifier.
side_effects: A logical timeout or clear that releases the physical owner can let late callbacks corrupt a replacement job.
A domain reload can erase in-memory TestRunStatus and operation-lock state while persisted TestRunner ownership remains.
Changing the project visibility map to strict deny-by-default would be a separate behavior migration and is not justified by this upstream range.
findings: Use persisted phases and a separate AwaitingRunStarted anchor; only an explicit Execute-return notification may start the initialization budget.
Persist one physical owner identity before Execute and validate it on every callback and terminal path.
Attach the effective dispatcher or batch lock to the job and retain it until a matching physical terminal; make clear_stuck a parameter-aware recovery path.
Forward explicit tokens through Python preflight/refresh and clear_stuck while preserving the existing exact tool visibility and annotation sets.

dispositions.resolution: Add the Website run_tests reference and CLI --clear-stuck help to scope; both must state that logical recovery does not release the physical fence and safe_to_start_new_run=false requires waiting for matching terminal state or restarting Unity.

business_invariants.statement: At most one force-persisted TestRunner owner identity (job_id + generation) exists. Every callback, task completion, reload recovery and terminal mutation names and compares that identity; no path guesses ownership from the newest logical job.

Job creation, queueing, semaphore wait and synchronous Execute duration never consume init_timeout. The budget starts only on an explicit matching Execute-return transition to AwaitingRunStarted; RunStarted with unknown total still transitions to Running.

The effective command or batch lock token is attached to the persisted test job before the start response completes. Command cleanup cannot release an attached lock; ordinary commands cannot Reenter or release it; only matching lifecycle recovery may inspect it and only a durably persisted physical terminal detaches or releases it. An unexpired explicit command lock survives dirty-preflight domain reload, while an unattached auto lock never does. Unattached locks are released on sync and async failures.

Matching physical completion is first written durably with the owner identity and terminal state. If that critical write fails, in-memory owner/status, TestRunStatus, callback binding and attached lock remain fenced and no queued successor is dispatched.

clear_stuck bypasses ordinary start filters, preflight and command-lock acquisition, but a timeout or clear never pretends to cancel an unproven physical run. It may terminate a queued ownerless job; otherwise it retains owner, TestRunStatus and lock and reports safe_to_start_new_run=false. manage_editor_lock force_release refuses while such an owner is attached and reports that the fence remains active.

After domain reload, the first readiness, PlayMode-options or command-guard consumer observes state only after an idempotent eager bootstrap restores persisted physical owner, callback registration, TestRunStatus and attached lock. Legacy V1 current-running state becomes a conservative owner with no init anchor and never replays Execute.

A normal run_tests start is the last executable batch item. Validation rejects any later item before execution; after a successful job start the outer token belongs only to that job and the batch cannot continue or reuse it. clear_stuck is not classified as a start.

The exact production C# tool-name set remains the 36 names present at local baseline 9d8751f18315e26d8cd97a4ab54d844d43b85fad, ProjectToolConfig remains an override map whose unlisted tools use EditorPrefs then metadata, manage_gameobject remains outside the C# high-risk lock classifier, run_tests/manage_gameobject/execute_code remain gated destructive server tools, group:* and tool:* visibility tags remain merged, and explicit editor_lock_token flows through dirty preflight refresh and clear_stuck without changing calls that omit it.

write_entry_table.entry: RunTests.HandleCommand creates and force-persists a Queued job, attaches the effective lock, schedules main-thread dispatch and returns job_id before runner invocation.
TryDispatchQueuedJob atomically claims owner and Dispatching, force-persists that state, then and only then invokes the job-bound runner; a failed critical persist invokes no runner.

The production RunTestsAsync path sends OnExecuteReturned(identity) only after its semaphore is acquired and TestRunnerApi.Execute has returned; the manager CASes Dispatching to AwaitingRunStarted and writes the anchor.

Identity-aware RunStarted, TestStarted, TestFinished and late task/callback paths update only the matching physical owner; RunStarted with unknown total still enters Running and duplicate or stale identities are ignored.
write_entry_table.exclusivity_note: This RED uniquely covers callback identity and stale/duplicate callback rejection; terminal persistence failure has a separate entry and RED.

write_entry_table.entry: FinalizePhysicalOwner constructs and force-persists the matching terminal snapshot before committing in-memory terminal status, clearing owner/callback state, releasing the attached lock or dispatching a queued successor; persist failure preserves every fence.
write_entry_table.exclusivity_note: This fault-injection RED uniquely covers the dangerous terminal-persist failure direction; normal finalization tests cannot substitute for it.

write_entry_table.entry: GetJob initialization timeout and ClearStuckJob may mark logical failure, but preserve nonterminal physical owner, TestRunStatus and attached lock until matching completion; an ownerless Queued job can terminate and release safely.

The existing TestJobManager class is an InitializeOnLoad bootstrap and exposes idempotent EnsureInitialized; the first readiness, PlayModeOptionsGuard or dispatcher consumer invokes it before observing state, restoring V2 owner, callback service, TestRunStatus and attached lock in that order.
write_entry_table.exclusivity_note: The test seeds persisted state and begins at a readiness consumer without first touching TestJobManager, so direct-manager restore tests cannot satisfy it.

write_entry_table.entry: Legacy V1 current+running state migrates once to a conservative physical owner with a new generation, Running phase, null AwaitingRunStarted anchor and no queued Execute replay.

AttachToJob atomically changes ownership without replacing the token; dispatcher/batch cleanup skips attached state, and a matching durably persisted terminal releases auto ownership or detaches explicit ownership according to its unexpired caller lease.

Reenter and Release reject an explicit token while it is attached to a physical job when invoked by an ordinary command; only identity-matching lifecycle recovery/finalization APIs can inspect or detach it.

Acquire/Extend/Release persist only an unexpired explicit command lease; reload restores an attached physical-owner lock first, otherwise restores that explicit lease, and never restores an unattached auto lock. The restored explicit token can pass dirty preflight refresh and then attach to its job.

The direct dispatcher classifies clear_stuck separately, forwards the effective token to run_tests, rejects ordinary use of an attached token, skips cleanup only after a verified attachment and releases a still-command-owned auto lock when registry invocation throws.

Batch preflight treats a normal run_tests request as a start and requires it to be the final executable item; after that item returns a job and attaches the outer token the batch terminates, while clear_stuck remains a recovery action that does not transfer the batch lock.
force_release refuses while SharedEditorOperationLock is attached to a persisted physical test owner and returns an explicit fence-active consequence; it cannot impersonate physical cancellation.

phase_table.meaning: Job and effective lock attachment are persisted and job_id may be returned; no physical owner exists, the run_tests batch item is terminal for its batch, and a reload may reschedule once.
phase_table.exits: Critical owner claim persists successfully and enters Dispatching, or ownerless clear/cancel durably enters Terminal.

phase_table.meaning: Physical owner is force-persisted and may be waiting for the service semaphore or inside synchronous Execute; init anchor is null and reload must not replay Execute.
phase_table.exits: Matching RunStarted enters Running, Execute return enters AwaitingRunStarted, or dispatch fault enters Terminal.

phase_table.meaning: Execute returned for the matching owner and the independent initialization anchor is set.
phase_table.exits: Matching RunStarted enters Running; timeout may mark logical failure but retains this physical fence; matching physical terminal enters Terminal.

phase_table.meaning: Matching RunStarted arrived, including a null test tree/unknown total; callbacks update only this owner.
phase_table.exits: Matching physical completion persists Terminal; logical clear may mark failed but cannot release the fence.

phase_table.meaning: Physical completion or an ownerless pre-dispatch cancellation is durably recorded before any in-memory owner/status mutation; only after that barrier may the matching job lock release/detach, TestRunStatus clear and a successor dispatch.
phase_table.exits: Terminal and idempotent; later callbacks or task continuations are ignored by identity/CAS. Persist failure leaves the prior nonterminal phase fully fenced.
